properties.name: easygram.messaging.type
properties.description: Role of this bot in broker integration: PRODUCER (publish updates) or CONSUMER (receive updates from broker). Omit entirely for standalone bots.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.forward-only
properties.description: When true, updates are published to the broker and local handlers are skipped. Only meaningful when messaging.type=PRODUCER.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.producer.type
properties.description: Broker backend for publishing updates. Required when messaging.type=PRODUCER.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.consumer.type
properties.description: Broker backend for consuming updates. Required when messaging.type=CONSUMER.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.topic
properties.description: Kafka topic name to publish to (PRODUCER) or consume from (CONSUMER). Required.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.group-id
properties.description: Kafka consumer group ID. Defaults to easygram-bot.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.create-if-absent
properties.description: Auto-create the Kafka topic when it does not exist. Requires broker admin permissions.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.partitions
properties.description: Number of partitions for the auto-created Kafka topic.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.replication-factor
properties.description: Replication factor for the auto-created Kafka topic.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.exchange
properties.description: RabbitMQ exchange name to publish to or bind the queue to. Required.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.queue
properties.description: RabbitMQ queue name for bot updates.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.routing-key
properties.description: Routing key used when publishing messages to the exchange.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.create-if-absent
properties.description: Auto-declare exchange, queue, and binding when they do not exist.

values.description: Publish Telegram updates to a message broker (Kafka or RabbitMQ).
Consume updates from a message broker; no direct Telegram transport is started.
